findings.reason: Confirmed, and reproduced. I checked each element rather than accept the report's. RS-07 does narrow AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3 with SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2 among its suppliedBy, its AN.3 reason does read 'Remove the old AN.3 -> SV.2 edge before adding SV.2 -> AN.3', its SV.2 reason does say 'Delete the old requires AN.3: this foundational inequality stage does not depend on zero-density estimates', and its link SV.2 -> AN.3 carries 'apply only after deleting the old reverse AN.3 -> SV.2 edge'. In the live atlas the reversal has not happened: SV.2's requires still holds AN.3, AN.3's consumers still holds SV.2, and SV.2 -> AN.3 appears in neither AN.3's requires nor SV.2's consumers. Running apply_restructurings read-only against data/atlas.json, with RS-07 alone and with all promoted proposals, reproduces the report's numbers exactly: 31 and 29 new stage edges respectively, AN.3 carrying restructured action 'narrow' with SV.2 in suppliedBy, the old edge present, the new edge absent, and ['SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2', 'AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3'] in skippedLinks both times. The skip is the cycle guard rather than the unknown-endpoint branch, since both endpoints are real stages. Medium is right: the accepted narrowing is in force while the supplier edge that was to replace the removed dependency is dropped, so the built graph is not the accepted one. The fix is right, including its refusal to fabricate stage nodes for UPSTREAM addresses and its instruction that appending the reverse edge to the old graph does not implement the plan. Two things to add for the fixer. First, a caution about regression tests. This proposal's skippedLinks has seventeen entries and only one is the defect; the other sixteen are UPSTREAM library addresses skipped by the earlier branch because they are not atlas stages, which is by design. A test asserting that RS-07 skips no links would therefore fail on correct behaviour — unlike RS-15, whose skippedLinks is the single cycle-guard entry, so that the 'no skipped links' assertion proposed there is right for RS-15 and wrong here. The assertion to carry across both is narrower: no link whose two endpoints are both stages may be skipped. Second, on coordination, which the finding already asks for and which I would now put more strongly. This is the second confirmed instance of one mechanism, and the mechanism is in the engine, not in either proposal: apply_restructurings writes a proposal's layer actions before processing its links and cannot undo them, so a proposal whose cycle-closing link is skipped keeps a narrowing whose precondition was never applied. Fixing two edge ledgers by hand leaves the next proposal to fail the same way; the engine should refuse to apply a proposal's narrowings when a both-endpoints-are-stages link is skipped, and fail loudly. Disclosure: I verified RT-RS-15/1 earlier in this session and confirmed it, reading scripts/restructure.py and running the same reproducer there. That is a different deliverable and I wrote neither red team, but this finding cites RS-15 and my reading of the shared mechanism comes from that job, so a reader should know the two verifications are not independent as to the mechanism. They are independent as to this instance: the RS-07 edges, decisions and reproducer output above were checked here from scratch.
